id.description: Stable slug used as the tool label everywhere (extension, collector, scanner, Loki, metrics).

license_group.description: Tools sold as one licence share a group: a seat that covers one of them covers the others (claude and claude-code, chatgpt and codex-cli). The portal's Budget view uses it to suggest what a subscription covers and to spot the same licence linked twice. Absence means the tool is licensed alone.

approved.description: true = sanctioned in your organisation. Records a governance position and does not affect finding severity: severity depends on the account domain, not on approval.

domains.description: eTLD+1 or subdomain, no scheme, no path. Consumed by extension, S1 scanner, discovery diff.

login_selector.description: Optional CSS selector hint for the extension to locate the account email in the DOM.

bundle_ids.description: macOS app bundle IDs (Jamf/collector) e.g. com.anthropic.claudefordesktop

app_names.description: macOS .app names and Windows display names for inventory matching.

config_paths.description: Paths relative to $HOME that indicate the tool is present.

account_json_path.description: File holding the account identity, if the tool stores one.

account_json_keys.description: Key path within account_json_path to the email, e.g. ["oauthAccount","emailAddress"].

account_jwt_path.description: Key path within account_json_path to a JWT string, e.g. ["tokens","id_token"]. Use instead of account_json_keys when the tool stores the identity inside a token rather than a plain field.

account_jwt_claim.description: Claim inside the decoded JWT payload holding the email, e.g. "email".

mcp_config_paths.description: MCP config paths valid on any OS, relative to the user's home. Use the _macos/_windows variants when the location differs per platform.

email_senders.description: Signup/verification sender domains for the Exchange scanner.

risk_tier.description: Default risk assessment. Carried from the CLI registry; used to prioritise triage, not to gate alerts.

entra_app_ids.description: Entra ID application/client IDs, matched against sign-in logs by the Entra scanner.

exe_names.description: Windows executable names for Intune inventory matching.

mcp_identifiers.description: MCP server names/slugs this tool exposes or connects as.

mcp_config_paths_macos.description: MCP config paths that exist only on macOS, relative to $HOME.

mcp_config_paths_linux.description: MCP config paths that exist only on Linux, relative to $HOME.

mcp_config_paths_windows.description: MCP config paths that exist only on Windows, relative to the user profile.

bridge_targets.description: SaaS services that should only be reached by browsers. A non-browser process connecting indicates an MCP bridge or API-token integration.

allowed_processes.description: Processes that legitimately reach bridge targets: browsers, native SaaS apps, system daemons. Anything else triggers a bridge finding.

discover_exclude_domains.description: Domains that match AI keywords but are not AI services. Filtered out by the discovery job.

relativePath.description: A path relative to the user's home directory. The collectors run as root or SYSTEM and join these to a home directory before reading them, so absolute paths, drive letters, parent traversal and control characters are refused here rather than trusted there.
